messages:
incident-bot: Paging maya_oncall: high error rate detected on /v1/generate in us-west-2 (5xx spike > 20% over 2m). Automatically escalated to P1. Logs attached.

maya_oncall: Acknowledged. Looking now. Any known deploys?

sam_eng: no deploys from infra in the last 10m, I see a surge of OOM in model-worker-7 and lots of 504s from the gateway.

marco_sre: I'm seeing a KV cache thrash on the serving nodes -> large CPU + IO. Rolling a quick config bump to reduce batch window (from 50ms to 20ms) to drop memory pressure. Pushing change now.

olivia_pdm: Heads-up: customer support already getting DMs about timeouts. We should prepare a short status page update. Can one of you draft copy? Keep it concise: impact, affected endpoints, mitigation, ETA.

maya_oncall: Marco's change applied. Initial CPU and error rates trending down but still elevated. ETA for stable baseline ~15m.

sam_eng: +1 on status update. Also suggests setting a fallback model for high-latency requests to reduce errors (route to small-quant model-xx-qa for non-critical requests). If we do that, need product signoff for behavior change.

olivia_pdm: Product OK with temporary fallback for non-enterprise tiers. Can we limit to anonymous/low-tier routes?

marco_sre: yes. I'll add routing rule: if latency > 1.2s then route to model-xx-qa for requests without enterprise feature flag. Deploying in 2m.

jessica_support: Draft for status page please — support will paste it into customer channels once published. Need plain language.

maya_oncall: Draft below, please review. (copy block)

statuspage-draft:
```
Short summary: We are investigating elevated error rates and timeouts for text generation requests in our us-west-2 region. Some requests to /v1/generate may fail or return delayed responses.

Impact: A subset of text generation requests (non-enterprise accounts and requests meeting high-latency conditions) may receive errors or be routed to a lower-latency fallback model. Enterprise customers with pinned capacity are not expected to be affected.

Mitigation: We have applied a temporary routing rule and reduced batch window to relieve memory pressure. Error rates are decreasing; monitoring continues. No data loss is expected.

Next update: We will provide another update within 15 minutes or sooner if the situation changes.
```

sam_eng: Copy reads well. Suggest small edit to impact line to call out endpoint path explicitly: "/v1/generate" — helps Support search.

olivia_pdm: +1. Also add note: "If you rely on latency-sensitive flows, consider retrying with exponential backoff for 10s."

maya_oncall: Updated draft with those edits. statuspage-bot, publish initial update to status page as "Investigating"?

statuspage-bot: Published initial update to Status Page (Investigating). Link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/21025. Notifying subscribers.

olivia_pdm: Thanks. Support copied into customer channels.

marco_sre: Monitoring graphs show error rate drop to 6% from 24% after routing rule. Still watching slow tails.

maya_oncall: Follow-up: We'll keep the routing rule for 30m and check memory metrics. If stable for 10m, we'll move to "Identified" with more detail.

sam_eng: Quick heads-up — I'm rolling a small rollback of a recent model-quant change on worker pool 7 as a precaution (non-disruptive, gradual).

olivia_pdm: Please add a short periodic update to status page once we hit stable baseline. I'll coordinate customer comms.

statuspage-bot: Update posted (Identified): "Root cause narrowed to memory pressure on serving nodes causing KV cache thrash. Temporary routing to a fallback model applied for non-enterprise traffic to maintain availability. Engineers are rolling a targeted rollback and tuning batch window. Estimated full resolution in 30-45 minutes."

jessica_support: Support copies updated message into public-facing channels and informs top impacted customers with suggested mitigations.

marco_sre: Memory and IO normalized after rollback and batch-window change. Error rate ~1.1% and latency p95 within normal bounds.

maya_oncall: Performing final validation sweeps across regions, will remove routing rule after 10m of stable metrics.

olivia_pdm: Preparing resolved notice. Draft below.

resolved-draft:
```
We have resolved the elevated error rates and timeouts affecting /v1/generate in us-west-2. The issue was caused by memory pressure and KV cache thrash on a subset of serving nodes. We applied a short-lived routing rule to a fallback model and rolled back a recent change to a worker pool; metrics have returned to normal.

Impact: For a short period, some text generation requests may have been delayed or returned errors. No data was lost. Enterprise pinned capacity customers were unaffected.

What we’re doing next: Post-incident review and a follow-up with engineering changes to prevent similar KV thrash scenarios. We will share a postmortem within 72 hours.
```

sam_eng: Looks good. +1 from eng.

statuspage-bot: Published resolved notice and closed the incident on the Status Page. Link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/21025/resolved

maya_oncall: Handing off to marcela for postmortem and timeline collection. Incident closed for oncall.

olivia_pdm: Thanks all. Support to follow up with customers who reported issues. I'll draft the 72h postmortem summary. :thumbsup:

jessica_support: Confirmed — notified impacted customers and added notes in the support tracker.

marco_sre: Leaving a few follow-up actions in the incident tracker (kernel tuning, KV cache backpressure controls).

maya_oncall: Ending thread — feel free to reopen if anything regresses.
